# Original interface Nat first study

This is an informed study, not a blind benchmark. The two first desired
sources use `classical fn` with a static Nat parameter. The actual prior CLI
refuses both at the parser. Preserve those sources, their first prediction and
both real diagnostics unchanged. The prediction's `not run` status records
the initial freeze; the separate observation records its later execution.

The separate translations change only that function prefix to `unitary fn`.
They pass parsing and reach the existing finite static-Nat profile refusal.
Neither translation is successful generic admission. Both have zero authored
qubits. No maximum-size case or new general static language is involved.

The private closure regression separately binds original parameter/result Nat
plans to normalized closed interface types. An ordinary `(n+n)-n-n` expression
must detect its u32 intermediate overflow for `n=2147483648`. A checked affine
helper retains its existing signed i128 template and final u32 contract.
These experiments do not submit a new generic source for native acceptance.

The observed Git HEAD and selected prior binary digest are separate identities;
this is not a clean commit-to-binary build attestation. Input, binary and kernel
stability were observed for each pair of calls. Full stdout/stderr are retained.
The bounded retention reader never executes recorded commands or source.
No source-preservation theorem, Meaning discharge, new scoped guarantee,
release approval or full QS/PR/RS/EXACT discharge is claimed.
